title: Proposition A: Referendum on House Bill 1 (2025 Congressional Map)

context.text: Citizen referendum petition (2026-R004) organized by People Not Politicians against House Bill 1 of the 2025 second extraordinary session, which the legislature passed in September 2025 and Gov. Mike Kehoe signed on September 28, 2025. The campaign delivered more than 300,000 signatures on December 9, 2025. Secretary of State Denny Hoskins rejected the referendum on August 4, 2026; on September 3, 2026 the Missouri Supreme Court unanimously ordered it certified and placed on the November ballot and barred use of the HB 1 map unless voters approve it. The 2022 map governs the November 2026 election.

question.text: Do the people of the state of Missouri approve the act of the General Assembly entitled “House Bill No. 1 (2025 Second Extraordinary Session),” which repeals Missouri’s existing congressional plan, and replaces it with new congressional boundaries that keep more counties intact? State and local governmental entities estimate no costs or savings.

summary.text: A yes vote approves House Bill 1, which redraws Missouri's eight congressional districts; a no vote repeals it and leaves in place the boundaries enacted in 2022. Ballotpedia and news reports describe the HB 1 map as dividing the Kansas City-based 5th District and giving Republicans an advantage in seven of eight districts, compared with six under the 2022 map. Per the Fair Ballot Language the measure would have no impact on taxes; state and local governmental entities estimate no costs or savings.

measure.yesMeans: “A ‘yes’ vote will approve the act of the General Assembly entitled ‘House Bill No. 1 (2025 Extraordinary Session),’ which redraws the congressional district boundaries.” (Secretary of State, Fair Ballot Language)
measure.noMeans: “A ‘no’ vote will leave in place the congressional district boundaries enacted in 2022.” (Secretary of State, Fair Ballot Language)

argumentsFor.text: Gov. Mike Kehoe, who called the special session, said after the Supreme Court's ruling: "I think the legislature did a good job passing what was a more fair and balanced map for Missouri. The courts didn't see it that way." He also called it "a map that represents Missouri's values much better than what we had."

argumentsAgainst.text: People Not Politicians (campaign for a No vote): "Politicians shouldn't be slicing and dicing communities to pick their voters — voters should be picking their politicians."

researchNotes: Official ballot title, fiscal statement and Fair Ballot Language are quoted verbatim (machine-checked) from the Missouri Secretary of State's certified-measure page. Missouri publishes no state voter pamphlet with pro/con arguments, so arguments are from campaign materials and news reports. In a veto referendum a Yes vote upholds the law, so a yes vote on Proposition A approves HB 1. The registered yes committee is Put Missouri First (about $3.1 million, mostly national Republican groups per Ballotpedia); its website returned HTTP 403 and was not bypassed, so the pro argument is the governor's statement rather than a campaign statement and each side has one statement (a second People Not Politicians quote from the Missouri Independent was dropped to match). The Ballotpedia summary of the map's partisan effect is attributed to news reports it quotes, and the U.S. Supreme Court's action blocking use of the 2025 map in 2026 is from the KCUR report.
